title: Register for joint-preserving and joint-replacing surgical procedures of the hip joint
summary:
The number of operations to implant an artificial hip joint continues to rise. In the future, there will be more and more patients to care for, so the number of revision surgeries in which the artificial joint or parts of it are replaced is also increasing. These joint-replacing operations are called endoprosthetic operations.
In addition, there are other diseases of the hip joint that are treated surgically in various ways, usually to avoid or at least delay joint replacement, i.e. these are joint-preserving operations.
Various national study registries have been documenting endoprosthetic procedures on knee and hip joints for years, primarily recording demographic data as well as revision procedures. Outcomes describing the function of hip replacement surgery are only collected in monocentric registry studies or multicenter studies with a clear research question.
To our knowledge, a registry study that includes functional and radiologic outcomes of hip preservation and hip replacement procedures and allows continuous follow-up of both groups or chronological transition from the joint preservation group to the cohort of joint replacement therapies is not yet available. 
As a university hospital, we perform many procedures on the hip, and the collection of comprehensive data on various surgeries should increase our knowledge of them. This is to adjust and improve treatment methods.
To achieve this, various data are collected and analyzed. Primarily, these are as follows: The times of initial implantation of a hip endoprosthesis and the time and thus the period until revision surgery and, in the case of joint-preserving surgery, likewise the times of this surgery and the time of any subsequent initial implantation of a hip endoprosthesis. Thus, the so-called standing times of the operations (and implants) are recorded.
In addition, X-ray images are evaluated and function and patient satisfaction are recorded using so-called scores (standardized questionnaires). 
In addition, complications are recorded so that these can also be evaluated. Appointments for follow-up are scheduled after 1 year, 2 years, 5 years and 10 years. Patients receive the same questionnaires, the so-called standardized scores, and are re-examined and, if necessary, x-rayed (also according to the routine) in accordance with the orthopedic routine for their intervention.
conditions: Pathology of the hip joint with indication for surgical treatment

interventions.name:

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with indication for the following surgeries:
- Primary endoprosthetic joint resurfacing of the hip.
- Aseptic and septic replacement surgery after hip endoprosthesis implantation (partial and total)
Femoral/ acetabular pathomorphologies (incl. femoral torsion defects) as well as hip joint dysplasia with indication for joint-preserving therapy
-periacetabular osteotomy
-femoral osteotomy
-mini-open arthrotomy/arthroscopy hip joint
Patients with indication for surgical treatment with the following diagnoses:
- Perthes disease
- Epiphysiolysis capitis femoris 
- Epiphyseal dysplasias
Exclusion criteria:
Patient request
